newsitem.title: USA: BPA still offers peak, on-peak, lowers most prices.
newsitem.headline: BPA still offers peak, on-peak, lowers most prices.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) continued to offer both peak and off-peak power for Tuesday pre-schedulings while slightly decreasing most of its prices, the agency said Monday.
BPA also offered "market expansion" power for the Northwest only at $9.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) for hours ending 0100-0500 and 2400 PST.

Tuesday firm power during off-peak hours was offered at $11.50 per MWh for all deliveries. Peak power was offerd at $16.75 (Northwest) and $17.75 (California-Oregon border), compared with $20.00 and $21.00, respectively, for Monday.
Tuesday non-firm power during off-peak hours was offered at $10.50-13.50 per MWh, while on-peak power was offered at $16.75-18.75 in the Northwest and $17.75-20.25 at COB.
